name: Should I hire a general handyman or an integrated remodeling contractor for turnover repairs?

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a general handyman or an integrated remodeling contractor for turnover repairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hiring an integrated remodeling contractor provides a single point of contact for multiple trades, whereas standard handypeople may handle only minor patches and lack finish carpentry or extensive tile skills. At HH Remodeling, Abraham Becerra personally oversees the site and handles drywall, trim, tile, and paint with his in-house crew, bringing in licensed plumbing or electrical sub-trades only when necessary. This saves property owners from managing separate dryivallers, painters, and tile setters on tight escrow or turnover deadlines.
acceptedAnswer.description: An integrated contractor manages drywall, carpentry, tile, and paint together under one point of contact, ensuring consistent finish quality on tight listing deadlines.
